expect.note: the newest committed evals/report/*-fast.json must report totals.wall_seconds within ADR-002 Decision 4's ceiling

provenance: the `fast` gate's wall clock went 13s (M2) -> 48.6s (M6) -> 55.4s (M7) -> 67.5s (M8) without one run ever turning red, because ADR-002 Decision 4's 60s ceiling was prose in an ADR and nothing read it. The breach was eventually noticed by a human reading a report, declared in ADR-009 Decision 6 and docs/support-matrix.md D8, and carried for two milestones. A budget nothing checks is a comment. Watched red before the M12 fix: the newest committed report (evals/report/20260821-021051-fast.json) measured wall_seconds 67.45 against budget 60, got.wall_seconds 67.45, passed false.

triage.note: grades the PREVIOUS run's committed report, because a suite cannot measure itself from inside. One run of lag is the whole cost, and it is far cheaper than the six milestones of lag the prose ceiling actually had. Deliberately NOT tagged `invariant`: invariants are absolute and machine-independent, and a wall clock is neither — ADR-009 Decision 6 records the same suite measuring 66.6-68.3s here and 68.6s on a reviewer's machine. This is a performance threshold that belongs to the baseline-gated suite, where a red run is a decision to make rather than a violation.
triage.not_covered: it cannot see a run that was never reported (`--no-report`, which is how the pre-commit hook runs), and it grades total wall clock only — a case that gets 10s slower while another gets 10s faster is invisible to it. Per-case timings are in the same report for anyone looking.
